title: Twenty-day two-mode fits predict two known KIC 5520878 combination signals with relative errors below 0.35 in Kepler Q11 to Q16
abstract: We test a local two-mode relation for two known combination signals of KIC 5520878. A complex response fitted in Kepler release 25 quarters 2 to 10 predicts quarters 11 to 16 with relative RMS errors of 0.174 to 0.345 in 20-day fits of aperture and corrected flux. Constant child coefficients give errors of 0.887 to 0.945. Ten-day and 30-day fits retain the prediction gain. An exact flux-to-magnitude test with both child terms removed does not reproduce the measured magnitude coefficients. The nearly steady primary limits the interpretation: a gain times the secondary alone predicts nearly as well. The result does not identify a physical coupling mechanism, a new mode, or a planet. Both flux products share exposures. Independent instrument confirmation is absent. Code, selected samples, input hashes, tables, controls, and reproduction instructions are included.

display.caption: Measured local amplitudes and predictions from the early complex response. The prediction test also uses phases, which are not shown. The vertical line marks the start of Q11. Q1 and Q17 are shown but are not in the reported early-to-later error.
